title: I made an iPhone 'pass the butter' robot you can talk to, and everything runs on the phone
author: Grand_Sprinkles_2094
selftext:
I made an iPhone robot you can talk to, and everything runs on the phone (Parakeet + Apple Foundation Models(LLM) + Kokoro)

I built a small iPhone app with a toy robot in a 3D room. You tap the mic and tell it what to do: "pass the butter", "come here", "put the ball on the table". It works out the steps, walks over, picks things up and answers you out loud. There are no servers or API keys; everything runs on the phone.

**How it works:**

* **Speech to text:** NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3, run through FluidAudio's Core ML port.
* **Understanding and planning:** Apple's on-device Foundation Models.
   * A quick first call decides whether you're chatting, asking for something it can do, or asking for something it can't (jump, dance, eat the butter). If it can't, it says so instead of doing the nearest thing.
   * For real tasks, the model reads the room state (where the robot is, what it's holding, what's in reach) and writes a goal plus a list of steps.
* **Plan checking:** the small model doesn't always plan right on its own (8 of 17 test prompts at first). So the app plays each plan through a simple model of the room before the robot moves. If the plan doesn't reach the goal, the app works out the steps for the goal the model picked. With that, my test prompts went from 8 of 17 right to 17 of 17.
* **Text to speech:** Kokoro-82M with a male voice and a light metallic effect. The robot's mouth glows in time with the loudness of its voice.
* **3D:** SceneKit with real physics. The ball rolls, and the robot pushes things and carries one item at a time. "Come here" walks it to wherever you've moved the camera.

**Speed:** on an iPhone 17, a chat reply takes about 1.5 s and an action plan about 4 s before the robot starts moving. Getting there took:

* loading each model session's instructions ahead of time;
* writing the robot's reply while it walks;
* dropping a "try again" round that cost about 3 s and rarely helped.

**Known issues:**

* About 600 MB of models download on first launch.
* FluidAudio warns that Kokoro can crash on iOS 27 after long sessions.
* The 3B on-device model sometimes adds a bit of made-up colour to replies.

It needs an iPhone with Apple Intelligence and Xcode 27. Code: [https://github.com/sujantr/RobotRoom](https://github.com/sujantr/RobotRoom)

I'd love feedback, especially on making the on-device planning faster.

comments.author: frindenolms
comments.body: It's a fun project, but that's all there is. fun project. What's the point of this app? you'll get bored instantly.

replies.author: Grand_Sprinkles_2094
replies.body: Yeah, just a fun project. No any real use cases. We could use this idea to put on the real game where this robot(or any character) you can talk to it and ask for help, make it work, kill the enemies, make it dance, etc. I don't know, still a new concept though.
